solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Awful rainproof hats — lacking originality, in a manner of speaking?

definitions.text: lacking originality, in a manner of speaking?

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of these two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a batch of rainproof hats is dreadful and unoriginal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase meaning by rote repetition, with the question mark because 'in a manner of speaking' is literally how a parrot talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating words mechanically without understanding, like a parrot, shows a lack of originality in speech.

clue.text: Fairy with something tiny, a gem

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or elf in Persian mythology
a dot is a very small thing

explanation.surface: A fairy appears holding a tiny jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of the mineral olivine.

clue.text: Swimmer with dyed hairstyle

parts.note: hair dyed red, taken as the colour
a mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A swimmer turns up with a hairdo coloured from a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is a common crossword way of saying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a fish of the Mediterranean and Atlantic, prized as food.

clue.text: Nymph that's old to get stuck in a book?

parts.words: to get stuck in a book
parts.note: to be engrossed in a book is to read

explanation.surface: An aged nymph is pictured absorbed in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology an oread is a mountain nymph.

clue.text: Time of abstinence with need somehow to be secure?

parts.note: a fast is a period of going without food

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of need are arranged in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a period of fasting combined with need makes a person secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fastened is fixed firmly in place, which is the adjectival sense of secure.

clue.text: Attempt to engage worker in song?

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so the worker goes inside the attempt

parts.note: a shy is a try or throw, as at a coconut shy
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A boss tries to hire a labourer for a singing job.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a rhythmic work song once sung by sailors.

clue.text: Learning a bit of English — it's tricky, usually

indicators.note: tricky means awkward to handle, so these letters are twisted into a new order
a bit of a word here is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A student remarks that learning English is usually a tricky business.
explanation.walkthrough: Add E, the first letter of 'English', to LEARNING and rearrange the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a rule or for the most part, the same as ordinarily.

clue.text: Child of immigrants that is evil in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
sin is wrongdoing or evil

explanation.surface: A sentence about an immigrant's child, linked with wickedness in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: IE + SIN read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisei is a Japanese term for a person born in America to parents who came from Japan.

clue.text: Cluster in marathon? Yours truly is last

indicators.note: is last puts the speaker's word at the end, after the race

parts.note: a marathon is a long-distance race
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: Someone in a pack of marathon runners admits finishing at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a botanical term for a flower cluster on short stalks along a central stem.

clue.text: Soldiers needing attire to be correct

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
dress means clothing

explanation.surface: Troops need proper uniform before they pass inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong or imbalance is to put it right.

clue.text: Imposing area in state capital

parts.note: august means grand or majestic

explanation.surface: An impressive district within a state's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital city of the US state of Maine.

clue.text: Doctor associated with university, I had become priest

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A university doctor explains how they took holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A druid was a priest of the ancient Celtic religion.

clue.text: One very reduced that's no longer uneasy about being huge

parts.note: ex describes something that once was, a former thing

indicators.note: about means around, so tense goes round the other letters

parts.note: tense means nervous or uneasy
I is the Roman numeral for one
very cut down to its abbreviation, V

explanation.surface: A cryptic sentence about someone once anxious and now unworried about being enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' tells you to abbreviate 'very' to V; 'that's no longer' is a roundabout way of saying former, ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive means covering a large area or scope, a close synonym for very big.

clue.text: Gifted Edward keeping a holy fast

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so Ted holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A clever man named Edward observes the religious fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means having natural ability, which is what being gifted means.

clue.text: Possible laundry items near running water

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: running means flowing and moving about, so the letters of water are rearranged

explanation.surface: Washing hung out beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running water' looks like a river; 'running' is the anagram signal on WATER, giving TWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are clothes that end up in the wash, so they are possible items for the laundry basket.

clue.text: Singer to quiver, maiden being put off

indicators.note: being put off means sent away, so the maiden's letter is removed

parts.note: to tremble is to quiver
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, one with no runs scored

explanation.surface: A performer starts shaking because a young woman has been driven away.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy singer with a high voice, the top part in a choir.

clue.text: Wild bear, not fat and grand, still alive

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters of bear are mixed up

parts.note: thin is the opposite of fat
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A wild bear, lean and magnificent, has survived.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAR rearranged gives BREA, followed by THIN and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that is breathing has not died yet, so it is living.

clue.text: Nasty b-bit of skeleton found in pit

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the stuttered bone sits within the pit

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
a rib is a bone of the skeleton, said with a stutter so its first letter doubles, as in b-bit

explanation.surface: A stammering report of a fragment of bones turning up in a hole, something grim.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'b-bit' tells you to stutter the bone too, doubling its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrible means very unpleasant or dreadful.

clue.text: Senility could make date go wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not as it should be, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: An old person's failing memory might make a meeting go awry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of old age marked by weakening mental powers.

clue.text: Refine little daughter, one up to now falling short

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: falling short means coming up one letter shy, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: still means even now, up to this time

explanation.surface: A parent wants to improve a young daughter who keeps failing to measure up.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil a liquid is to purify it by evaporation and condensation, a process of refining.

clue.text: Miners with dogs, right for protection

indicators.note: the dogs shelter the letter by enclosing it, giving protection

parts.note: collies are a breed of sheepdog

explanation.surface: Coal workers keep sheepdogs to guard their rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Colliers are men who work in coal mines.

clue.text: In a while dwarfish person will acquire length

indicators.note: acquire means take in, so the letter for length goes inside

parts.note: a shorty is an informal word for a small person

explanation.surface: A small person predicts growing taller before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly means soon or before long, after a short time.

clue.text: New mag — it's making a mark

indicators.note: new here means remade, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A freshly launched magazine is making its mark on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, and also a spot or scar on the skin.

clue.text: Component of a gate?

parts.note: a gate is the attendance at a sports match, so one of its members is a person watching, not a bar or hinge

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hinge or latch; in British sport the gate is the crowd at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person who pays to watch a match counts toward the attendance figure.

clue.text: Outcome of e.g. long jump

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a contest in an athletics meeting

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like asking what a jump produced; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a result or happening and a single competition in a sports programme.

clue.text: Saw wild area mostly keeping dry

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the shortened moor holds the dry letters
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a moor is an area of open uncultivated upland
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone saw an untamed stretch of land that had largely stayed parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb; here it is a noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, much like a maxim or motto.

clue.text: African mum's tiptop

parts.note: ma is mum, with the possessive s
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Someone praises an African mother as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Lettuce that is frozen solid?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crisp round variety of salad lettuce
second meaning: a huge floating mass of ice

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks if a lettuce has been left in the freezer; the two halves give separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a crunchy salad variety and to a great block of glacier ice adrift at sea.

clue.text: Bishop gets to help musician

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to assist is to help

explanation.surface: A bishop is allowed to give a hand to a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassist plays the bass guitar or double bass in a band.

clue.text: Ten try healing drunk displaying menacing manner

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and disordered, so the letters of the three words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ten people try to sober up a drunk who is behaving aggressively.
explanation.definitionFit: Threateningly is an adverb describing how someone acts when hostile and intimidating.
